 Dallas Wings star Paige Bueckers has won an award that exemplifies her community service. The WNBA announced on Thursday that Bueckers is the recipient of the 2026 Dawn Staley Community Leadership Award. The award was established in 2008, named after Staley, and recognizes players who represent a spirit of leadership, love for the game, charitable efforts, and inspiration.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Bueckers spoke about the honor in a statement released by the WNBA, saying, "With every partnership I take on, it's really important to me to include a charity or community engagement component. I've been fortunate to have so many people and communities invest in me throughout my life, and I want to pay that forward by using my platform to create opportunities for the next generation. Whether that's through sports, education, food security or mentorship, I want to make sure people have access to opportunities they might not otherwise have. Sports have given me so much, and I think they can be such a powerful way to bring people together, build community and create opportunity."
 Dawn Staley also spoke about Buecker's victory.

 "Paige Bueckers embodies the spirit of what this award, established in my name, represents. Through her leadership, compassion, and commitment to service, Paige uses her platform to uplift communities and inspire the next generation. I'm proud to honor her for making a difference that reaches far beyond basketball."
 Click Above to Subscribe On the court Bueckers had a stellar sophomore season campaign. She averaged 20.9 points, 4.1 rebounds, 5.9 assists, and 1 steal while shooting 31% from 3 in 42 games. Her play ultimately led her team to the WNBA playoffs, where they lost to the eventual WNBA champion Golden State Valkyries.
